problem:
3x - 5y = 8
kx + 20y = -32
In the given system of equations, k is a constant. If the system has infinitely many solutions, what is the value of k?

bad.why: Finding the multiplier 20/(-5) = -4 and applying it to 3 relies on the memorized rule that the equations must be multiples of each other; the overlapping graphs show it without the rule.
Checking each choice by hand for proportional coefficients and constants is four rounds of ratio work the slider shows in one drag.
Typed into Desmos, the same computation still needs the memorized rule that the equations are multiples of each other; the slider shows the lines coinciding.

algebraFirst.description: Uses the rule that the two equations must be multiples of each other: finds the factor 20/(-5) = -4 and multiplies 3 by it to get k = -12.

explanationNotes: Explain 'infinitely many solutions' as 'both equations draw the exact same line', so every point on it solves both. Dragging k swings the second line until it lies exactly on top of the first at k = -12; a merely parallel pair would instead mean no solution.
